newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's MTBE demand seen capped by new refinery.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's MTBE demand seen capped by new refinery.

text.p: Taiwan's demand for petroleum additive methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) could falter when the country's first private refinery comes onstream in 1999, a senior industry official said on Tuesday.
"There is no room for growth," said the official from Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC).
"Demand is increasing but it is not increasing like a few years ago as we are already including a lot of MTBE in the mogas we import," the official said.
MTBE is blended with gasoline to boost its octane number and replace environmentally-damaging lead.
Taiwan's consumption of MTBE is rising almost at the same rate as gasoline, which is rising three to four percent annually.

But production from the country's first private refinery, due onsteam in 1991, could dampen the need for MTBE because it will produce higher quality gasoline that will need less of the octane-booster.
Taiwan's industrial conglomerate Formosa Plastics Group will bring onstream a 21 million tonnes-a-year (450,000 barrels-per-day) refinery, which would include a 44,000 tonne-per-year MTBE plant.
"Formosa Plastic's new reformer will be able to produce very good gasoline which would not require too much MTBE. And it can cover its MTBE requirements from its own plant," said the CPC official.
Currently, Taiwan consumes up to 350,000 tonnes a year of MTBE but only produces 150,000 tonnes. CPC covers the shortfall with imports, mainly from the Middle East.
